scheme_name: A Program to Provide 90 Percent Assistance in Planting Material of Horticultural Fruit Crops
description:
The Indian government has initiated a welfare scheme aimed at enhancing the horticultural sector through the provision of financial assistance for planting material of horticultural fruit crops. 

This program is officially known as the "Program to Provide 90 Percent Assistance in Planting Material of Horticultural Fruit Crops." 

It was launched in the year 2014 under the National Horticulture Mission. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to promote the cultivation of horticultural fruit crops among farmers. 

The government aims to increase the area under horticulture cultivation by providing financial support. 

The specific goal is to enhance the production of fruits in India, thereby improving the income of farmers. 

The program targets to cover a minimum of 10,000 hectares of land across various states. 

The scheme provides 90 percent financial assistance to farmers for purchasing quality planting material. 

This assistance is crucial as it significantly reduces the financial burden on farmers. 

The maximum financial assistance provided under this scheme is capped at INR 1.5 lakh per hectare. 

Farmers can avail of this assistance for a variety of horticultural fruit crops. 

These crops include mango, banana, guava, papaya, and citrus fruits among others. 

The financial assistance is aimed at ensuring that farmers have access to high-quality planting material. 

This is essential for improving yield and ensuring better quality produce. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme are clearly defined. 

Farmers must be registered under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi scheme. 

They must also possess a valid landholding certificate. 

The age limit for applicants is set at a minimum of 18 years. 

There is no specific upper age limit for eligibility. 

The income criteria stipulate that farmers should have an annual income below INR 2 lakh. 

This ensures that the benefits reach the economically weaker sections of society. 

The application process is straightforward and designed to be farmer-friendly. 

Farmers need to visit their local horticulture department office to apply. 

They must fill out the application form provided by the department. 

The required documents include a copy of the landholding certificate. 

Farmers must also submit proof of identity such as an Aadhar card. 

Additionally, they need to provide bank account details for the disbursement of funds. 

Once the application is submitted, it is verified by the horticulture department officials. 

The verification process typically takes about 15 to 30 days. 

Upon successful verification, the financial assistance is disbursed directly to the farmer's bank account. 

The disbursement is usually done in one installment. 

Farmers are encouraged to utilize the funds within the stipulated time frame. 

The funds must be used specifically for purchasing planting material. 

The program is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The National Horticulture Board oversees the execution of this scheme. 

Farmers can contact the local horticulture department for any queries. 

The contact details for the department can usually be found on the official state government websites. 

The scheme has seen a positive response since its inception. 

As of 2023, over 50,000 farmers have benefited from this program. 

The total area covered under this scheme has exceeded 15,000 hectares. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 500 crores for the current financial year. 

This budget is aimed at expanding the reach of the program to more farmers. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of using disease-free and high-yielding varieties of planting material. 

This is crucial for ensuring sustainable agricultural practices. 

Farmers are also encouraged to participate in training programs organized by the horticulture department. 

These programs provide valuable information on best practices in horticulture. 

The government aims to improve the overall productivity of the horticultural sector through such initiatives. 

The scheme not only benefits individual farmers but also contributes to the national economy. 

Increased production of fruits can lead to better food security in the country. 

Moreover, it can enhance the export potential of Indian horticultural products. 

The government is also focusing on creating awareness about this scheme among farmers. 

Various outreach programs are conducted to educate farmers about the benefits. 

The use of technology is encouraged to streamline the application process. 

Farmers can also access information about the scheme through official mobile applications. 

The government is committed to improving the livelihoods of farmers through such welfare schemes. 

The success of this program can be measured by the increase in fruit production in the states where it has been implemented. 

The scheme is part of a larger strategy to promote sustainable agriculture in India. 

By providing financial assistance for planting material, the government aims to empower farmers. 

This empowerment is essential for achieving self-sufficiency in food production. 

The program is a significant step towards enhancing the horticultural landscape of India. 

Farmers are encouraged to take full advantage of this scheme to improve their agricultural practices. 

The long-term vision of the government is to make India a global leader in horticulture. 

This scheme plays a vital role in realizing that vision. 

In conclusion, the "Program to Provide 90 Percent Assistance in Planting Material of Horticultural Fruit Crops" is a comprehensive initiative aimed at uplifting the horticultural sector in India. 

It provides substantial financial assistance to farmers, thereby promoting sustainable agricultural practices and enhancing food security.
